answer: Latency terrace admission. Each identity must show a staggered arrival curve: requests spread across a delay terrace, not bursted at one instant. Agents building history on a knoll of steady traffic earn lower queue positions; sudden floods get throttled at the river of admission. Enforcement compares inter-arrival variance per identity against a rolling baseline; flat bursts trigger slowdown. An attacker pays real wall-clock time per identity, making mass registration linearly expensive.
